single_points.text: One reviewer says dying causes extreme punishment like losing the entire run, losing a level, and doing unnecessary backtracking to get souls before fighting the boss again.

citation.review_text:
Honestly, it's more of rogue-like than soul-like and time pressure is massive.
There is not enough time to read what the items even do, when you need to make the selection.
The map is uninspired, the tutorial doesn't even tell you what the icons on map mean.

And the worst part is that it's just unenjoyable. I don't have the time to see around the map or fight normal mobs becouse you are forced to rush bosses. No time to read items in shop or boss rewards. And the extreme punishment for dying often means losing the entire run. The stable of souls-like was
dying to boss -> running up to arena -> fight the boss again and optionally get your souls back.

Here you also lose 1 level, so you need to get souls back and then go to a fire, before finnaly fighting the boss again, which is a lot of unneccessary backtracting and costs a lot of time. Or you can fight the boss with 1 level down, which is harder and might straight up disable your weapon (they are level restricted).

Honestly, i still wouldn't mind it, if we had a mode with double the times and poor rewards so i can put the time and effort into learning the game myslef, but devs decided it's better to put a link to a guide in a menu and call it a day...

Overall 6/10

I enjoyed some time in this game but... 

a) it feels very "lazy" and unfinished - basically its Elden Ring models+combat , slightly expedited. The experiment in roguelite genre is welcome, but it doesn't come off as a game which got a lot of love - esp. post release. 
b) Even with a considerable rig, I REGULARLY dropped from 85->20FPS. I tried increasing shader size, tuning shadows, etc etc to no avail. The game is clearly unoptimised and that doesn't align with this studios normal quality.
Its a great game up until it stopped wanting to work, it crashes all the time, it freezes and i have no idea what to do if someone has a solution please lmk because ive exhausted most options

I really liked this game, but recently, it just crashes nonstop. I have so many modern games on my computer, and this is the only one that crashes. I can play for about 20 minutes, then the game crashes. I relaunch and it crashes when I rejoin my session, sometimes in the menu.

The only fix is to restart my computer and that just buys me another 20 minutes before I go back into the crashing cycle. Breaks my heart because I really enjoyed playing it. Beat several bosses, but as of last week, the game is broken for me.
I payed money for a game that doesn't work half the time and it makes the experience worse for everyone. everyday crashes really discourages from playing the game.

The game is pretty good but some EAC update completely broke it and a lot of people are now randomly crashing all the time (myself included). The game literally just turns off, no logs, nothing, and if you reconnect to the same session sometimes the game just instantly closes again, leaving the other players without a teammate and no way to rejoin.
it keeps on crashing for no reason

hi devs update ur game

I really don't want to recommend this game. As if there's a ghost of Miyazaki standing behind me getting ready to take his socks off if I don't recommend it.... So, I will. Not because of any foot related threats but because it's a good game. If any other studio made this game it would be a towering accomplishment. Here's the "But"..... BUT it's FromSoftware. 

Make a game with the title Elden Ring, attach a roguelite to it with asynchronous character classes that do unique things and you have a recipe for success. What we ended up getting was a complete lack of replayability because the upgrades are uninspired, ONE map pre-DLC, and variation so poor that you see pretty much everything within the first 10 hours of gameplay. 


There's a lot of good here but it is over-shadu'd by it's flaws.
The potential here is too damn high to let them off easy. It's fun, and modding helps fill the gaps. Yet a lot of us will wonder what could have been.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks long-term content updates and new expansions following its post-launch period.

citations.review_text:
It's a great game to play with friends; and I appreciate the Deep of Night update since it gives you a reason to keep grinding. 

Unfortunately, though, it's become clear that Nightreign was never meant to be a long-term game in the series. Rather, it's a quick cash grab by reusing as many assets as possible while dedicating the bare minimum development resources they could get away with. 

There hasn't been a single content update in almost a year and I'm fairly confident there won't ever be another. Now they'll just be watching the sales numbers to see when the revenue from the game falls beneath the cost to keep the servers running. When that happens I guess it's goodbye. This game deserves far more than the slow death they always planned for it to have.

The game simply doesn't care about the player's experience, either quantitatively or qualitatively. Let me explain.

In terms of quantity, the game has very little content, with a rather lackluster paid expansion released a few months after the game's launch (May 2025, December 2025). I'm writing this review in November 2026, and we still haven't seen anything new: no balance changes, no new skins, no new characters, no new weapons (the game is still missing all the weapons from Shadow of the Erdtree, which could easily be copy-pasted into Nightreign without too much trouble!). A huge disappointment.

In terms of quality, the game suffers from some serious design issues. The biggest one is onboarding and learning the maps. The game pushes you to do everything as quickly as possible. How am I supposed to learn the map if, in order to win and avoid getting wiped out on the first night, I have to rush through very specific locations so quickly that I can't even stop for a moment?
This has been particularly problematic with the new map, which for quite some time was a source of frustration whenever it appeared on screen, precisely because of its convoluted layout

Am I really supposed to watch YouTubers' gameplay videos? It's the equivalent of buying an IKEA piece of furniture that comes without instructions and then having to watch some guy on YouTube explain how to put it together. I want to have the manual and the tools to learn the map on my own. There's not even a free-roam mode, and there's absolutely no reason for that.

Another example of this disconnect between the speed and urgency the game demands and the knowledge the game itself requires can be found in certain moments when you acquire a new ability or item but literally don't have enough time to read its description and understand the tool you've just obtained.

This is a design philosophy that only works if the player base relies on YouTubers, streamers, and wikis. And there's nothing inherentl…

single_points.text: One reviewer states that runs become repetitive due to encountering the same map seeds, recycled field bosses, and predictable camp layouts.

citation.review_text:
The first dozen hours are an absolute blast. Taking Elden Ring's combat and cranking the speed up with wall jumps, distinct Nightfarer abilities, and frantic three day runs feels super fresh at first. Sprinting through Limveld with a squad to grab quick upgrades before the circle closes in creates some awesome, high energy boss fights against the Night Lords.

Unfortunately, the novelty wears off way faster than it should. Instead of true roguelike variety, you quickly start running into the exact same map seeds, recycled field bosses, and predictable camp layouts over and over. Once you learn the optimal routes to hit max level, every forty minute run starts blending together into a repetitive chore. It is a really fun remix for a weekend or two, especially if you love the base game's combat, but it just lacks the depth and randomness to stay enjoyable long term.
